subject.title: [Bug]: Hallucination Loop — Agent Generated Irrelevant Multi-Thousand-Word Responses Across 2 Simultaneous Sessions

question: For this Telegram direct-chat burst, should OpenClaw treat shared main-session DMs as expected configuration behavior, change the default or doctor/onboarding recovery toward isolated DMs, or add a runtime guard for irrelevant runaway output?
rationale: The evidence proves an operational burst and shows current shared-DM semantics, but the payload-free diagnostics do not identify whether the cause was configuration, route/session leakage, provider behavior, or a missing semantic safety policy.

options.title: Classify and narrow before fixing
options.body: Keep the issue open while a maintainer decides whether the repair belongs in DM isolation, Telegram route delivery, or output safety, then request only the evidence needed for that path.

options.title: Treat as configuration/support
options.body: If shared main-session DMs are accepted behavior, close after documenting the per-channel-peer requirement and asking for a fresh report only if it reproduces with isolated DM scope.

options.title: Route to broader output-finalization work
options.body: If maintainers decide the session routing is expected, link this as a field signal under the broader channel-output or hallucinated-output trackers instead of keeping a separate Telegram incident open.

recommendation.title: Classify and narrow before fixing
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while a maintainer decides whether the repair belongs in DM isolation, Telegram route delivery, or output safety, then request only the evidence needed for that path.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent history covers the dmScope documentation and outbound session-helper boundary, and this choice is more product/routing policy than a single mechanical bug fix.
